prompt: Many aspects of the way people dress today are influenced by global fashion trends. How has global fashion become such a strong influence on people’s lives? Do you think this is a positive or negative development? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay:
Nowadays, globalisation of fashion has become more and more prevalent among youths in the majority of countries. The increasing popularity of pop cultures and social media applications is considered to be a huge catalyst for this fashionglobalisation. However, I am in favour of the view that these trends can have adverse effects on the cultures of minority groups as well as their identity. The following paragraphs will delve into how fashion trends started to spread globally and why I believe that it can have drastic effects on local cultures.

This globalisation of clothing styles can be said to stem from the rise of pop cultures and social media platforms. World-famous singers and artists have millions of fans from all over the world, and they have the ability to influence their fans in many aspects of life. This is even more fuelled by the invention of applications such as Facebook and Instagram, which allow fans to catch up with what kind of styles their idols are adopting, and to imitate those immediately in their daily life. For example, if a picture of Taylor Swift wearing a plain white T-shirt while shopping circulated online, thousands of her fans across the world would definitely find it fashionable to wear those plain white T-shirts on a daily basis. If it had not been for social media and pop artists, this would never have happened.

On the other hand, it is concerning that this can put other minority cultures and fashion styles at risk. Seeing as many youths are a lot more into global cultures in fashion, it may become significantly challenging for locals to persuade the younger population to preserve their traditional styles. An obvious impact of this would be the loss of cultural identity, since global fashion trends took over. For instance, these days in Myanmar, most would rather choose to wear global designs such as denim jackets and hoodies than Myanmar traditional longyis made of cotton, which makes it hard for us to showcase the best of Myanmar cultural fashion styles to other foreign countries. If it were not for this globalisation, more Myanmar traditional costumes would still be seen in public places of our country.

To conclude, pop music and the internet contributed mainly to the surge in global fashion trends. Despite its popularity, I am still convinced that it can threaten the fashions of minority cultures. Doing awareness campaigns to promote local cultures and fashion might reduce its negative impact to some extent, thereby eliminating the concerns to loss of cultural value in fashion.
